title: Add data tests to your DAG
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Data tests are SELECT queries that return failing rows; zero rows passes; singular and generic tests; built-in unique, not_null, accepted_values and relationships; severity warn or error with warn_if and error_if; store_failures writes failing rows to an audit schema; tests: is now an alias of data_tests:.

title: Model contracts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Enforced contracts need every column's name and data_type and fail the build on mismatch; supported on table, view (no constraints) and incremental with on_schema_change append_new_columns or fail; not_null is the constraint most often enforced, primary and foreign keys often only recorded on cloud warehouses; breaking changes listed.

title: Configure incremental models
supports: Opened with WebFetch. is_incremental() conditions; without unique_key most adapters append and duplicate; unique_key must be unique and not null; >= filter and lookback windows; --full-refresh drops and rebuilds; on_schema_change defaults to ignore; Snowflake notice of September 2026 for dbt-snowflake below 1.10.6.

title: Add sources to your DAG (source freshness)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Freshness config with loaded_at_field and warn_after or error_after, inherited from source to table; freshness: null disables it; a filter limits the freshness query; in dbt v2 the command is dbt freshness --resource-type source and results go to target/freshness.json.

title: Source freshness
supports: Opened with WebFetch. dbt build does not include freshness checks; a freshness run step fails and stops later steps when data is stale; run freshness jobs at least twice as often as the shortest SLA; Snowflake freshness uses LAST_ALTERED.

title: Staging: preparing our atomic building blocks
publisher: dbt Developer Hub (dbt Labs), best practice guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Folders by source system; stg_[source]__[entity]s naming; staging models are the only place source() is used, one per source table; renaming, type casting, basic computations and categorising only; no joins or aggregations; materialise as views; base models as the exception.

title: Unit tests
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Available from dbt v1.8; given and expect rows test SQL logic before the model is built; use for complex logic, edge cases and refactors; dbt Labs recommends running them only in development or CI; SQL models in the current project only.

title: Add snapshots to your DAG
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Snapshots implement type 2 slowly changing dimensions; YAML config from v1.9; timestamp strategy recommended, check strategy when no reliable updated_at; dbt_valid_from and dbt_valid_to; hard_deletes ignore, invalidate or new_record; snapshots ignore full_refresh so history is kept.

title: About dbt versions
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 23 October 2026. dbt v2.0 released 14 September 2026 (dbt v2 and dbt OSS distributions); v1.12 released 16 July 2026, active support to 15 July 2027; v1.11 critical support until 18 December 2026; each minor supported one year; v1.3 to v1.7 deprecated in the platform on 31 January 2027.

title: About dbt MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Local server (uvx dbt-mcp) can run dbt run, build and test; remote server over HTTP cannot run CLI commands; tool groups for Semantic Layer, SQL, Discovery and Admin API; tools depend on plan; described as a read-only access layer that does not store production data.

title: Best Practices
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Treat tasks like database transactions; use UPSERT not INSERT on re-runs; read and write a specific partition keyed on data_interval_start; never use now() for critical computation; keep top-level DAG code light; XCom only for small messages; credentials in Connections or a secrets backend; test DAGs.

title: Supported versions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Airflow 3 current at 3.4.0, first released 22 April 2025; Airflow 2 (last 2.11.2) reached end of life on 22 April 2026 after limited maintenance from 22 October 2025.

title: DAG Runs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Catchup is off by default; backfill from the UI or airflow backfill create with a reprocess behaviour and max active runs; trigger timetables such as @daily have equal data_interval_start and end, data-interval timetables cover a window; clearing a task re-runs it.

title: Asset checks
supports: Opened with WebFetch (docs.dagster.io redirects here). Asset checks test one property of an asset; they run with jobs that target the asset or on their own schedule; a failed check does not stop downstream assets unless blocking=True.

title: Estimate and control costs
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no page date. Dry runs give an upper-bound estimate; maximum bytes billed fails a query without charge; custom daily quotas are a hard cap for on-demand; LIMIT does not reduce bytes read on non-clustered tables; preview tables instead of querying; Cloud Billing budgets and alerts.

title: Data retention with time travel and fail-safe
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Time travel covers 7 days by default, configurable from 2 to 7 days; fail-safe keeps deleted data 7 more days, recoverable only through Cloud Customer Care; deleted tables restored with a table copy using a timestamp decorator; storage billing model affects cost.

title: Introduction to partitioned tables
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Integer-range, time-unit column and ingestion-time partitioning; boundaries in UTC; partition expiration deletes whole partitions; prefer clustering when partitions would be small (roughly under 10 GB), filters span many columns or DML touches most partitions.

title: Use the BigQuery MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Tools list datasets and tables, get metadata, execute_sql and execute_sql_readonly; execute_sql is the only non-read-only tool; IAM deny policies can block it; queries cancelled after three minutes by default; results capped at 3,000 rows.

title: Working with resource monitors
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Resource monitors track warehouse credits and can notify, suspend or suspend immediately at thresholds; only ACCOUNTADMIN creates them; they do not cover serverless features or AI services (use budgets); suspension can lag, so set buffer thresholds.

title: Understanding & using Time Travel
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Default retention 1 day; Enterprise Edition allows 0 to 90 days for permanent objects; transient and temporary tables 0 or 1 day; AT and BEFORE clauses; UNDROP restores dropped objects; Fail-safe 7 days after Time Travel, recoverable only by Snowflake.

title: Warehouse considerations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Set auto-suspend low (for example 5 or 10 minutes or less) and matched to gaps in the workload; 60-second minimum billing each time a warehouse starts, then per second; larger sizes are not always faster; test sizes with the same queries.

title: Snowflake-managed MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Exposes Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, SQL execution and custom tools; OAuth recommended; permission is granted per tool; the SQL tool's read_only option defaults to true; restrict OAuth to a dedicated MCP role.

title: Open Data Contract Standard
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A YAML data contract with sections including fundamentals, schema, data quality, support and communication channels, pricing, team, roles, service-level agreement and servers; meant to be platform agnostic.

title: bitol-io/open-data-contract-standard
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Current version v3.2.0 (no release date shown); citation lists the LF AI & Data Foundation as the organisation.

title: Data Processing Pipelines (Site Reliability Workbook)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Pipeline SLOs for freshness, correctness, isolation and end-to-end; golden data; alerts linked to playbooks; stale data is almost always better than incorrect data; idempotent and two-phase mutations; Spotify event delivery case with timeliness, skewness and completeness SLOs.

title: PHE statement on delayed reporting of COVID-19 cases
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 4 October 2020: 15,841 cases between 25 September and 2 October were left out of reported figures because some files exceeded the maximum file size the loading system could handle; fixed by splitting large files and an end-to-end review.

title: Sync modes
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Soft delete mode marks deleted source rows as deleted; live mode keeps an exact copy of the source table; history mode keeps every version of a row; live and history modes only for some connectors.

title: Sync modes
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Full refresh overwrite, full refresh append, incremental append, incremental append plus deduped (a deduplicated view on a primary key) and full refresh overwrite plus deduped; incremental reads use a cursor or change data capture.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Article 5(1)(c) data minimisation ('adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary') and 5(1)(e) storage limitation (kept identifiable no longer than necessary).

title: Enable the BigQuery sandbox
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No credit card needed; 10 GiB storage (lifetime, not refunded on deletion) and 1 TiB of query processing a month; tables, views and partitions expire after 60 days; no streaming, DML or Data Transfer Service.
